top_story.headline: Health and Human Services books three Anthropic awards worth $9 million in one day for an 'enterprise wide chat bridge'
top_story.dek: Three records dated October 27 from the department's Office of the Assistant Secretary for Financial Resources name Anthropic, PBC as the recipient.
paragraphs: The Department of Health and Human Services (Office of the Assistant Secretary for Financial Resources) recorded three awards to Anthropic, PBC on October 27: $4,842,000, $3,573,000 and $585,000, which add up to exactly $9,000,000. All three carry the same description, 'ANTHROPIC SI ENTERPRISE WIDE CHAT BRIDGE', and are coded as software as a service for business applications under computer systems design services.

The amounts are what has been obligated so far on each base award. The records in today's data don't say whether the awards were competed, what 'SI' or 'bridge' refers to, or how many department staff will use the service. The two larger awards are in the $2 million-and-up tier and the $585,000 award is in the smaller tier.

sections.eyebrow: White House & Executive Office of the President
sections.headline: Nothing tied to the White House in today's contracting data
paragraphs: One item was tagged by the keyword match: a $12.5 million spacesuit delivery order to Axiom Space. It was awarded by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, not by an Executive Office of the President component, and nothing in its description ties it to presidential operations, so it is written up under USAspending Contracts.

sections.headline: NASA sole-sources nine lunar neutron spectrometers from Lockheed Martin, citing the race with China and a 2028 landing deadline
paragraphs: There are 35 new justifications today, 23 of them posted under other notice types such as Award Notice and Special Notice; 5 repeats from earlier editions were left out. Three are extensions and appear in the next section. The rest are mostly Defense Department and Veterans Affairs buys from the original maker.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: NASA buys nine lunar neutron spectrometers from Lockheed Martin without competition, citing the race with China
meta: Urgent need, no time to compete
National Aeronautics and Space Administration (Ames Research Center)
blocks.text: The nine build-to-print instruments are for Moon Base Phase I robotic missions, including the MoonFall lunar drone project and the CS-8 multi-lander project, with one spare. The justification says the Artemis program must return astronauts to the Moon before China, cites Executive Order 14369 (Ensuring American Space Superiority) and a 2028 landing goal, and notes Lockheed Martin built six earlier units under prior NASA awards. It was posted as an Award Notice.

blocks.title: Air Force buys $2.96 million of B-1B electronic warfare simulator support from Keysight without competition
meta: Only one company can do it
blocks.text: The three-year purchase order (12-month base plus two option years) covers calibration and repair, Simulation View licenses, expert support and a customized calibration cart for the B-1B Electronic Warfare Advanced Simulation Platform. The justification says Keysight Technologies is the developer and sole proprietor of the system's design, source code and hardware, and that anyone else would mean a new system and 'a substantial duplication of cost'.

sections.headline: Navy extends a Naval Air Forces administrative support contract eight months while two Government Accountability Office protests play out
paragraphs: Three new extensions today: a Navy bridge, a Transportation Department cybersecurity extension and a General Services Administration lease extension.

blocks.title: Navy bridges its Naval Air Forces administrative support contract for eight months during a protest corrective action
meta: Urgent need, no time to compete
Department of the Navy (Fleet Logistics Center San Diego)
blocks.text: The cost-plus bridge adds a four-month base and a four-month option for Virtual Computing Technology, which has 215 staff across 14 squadrons and two headquarters providing mail, personnel and travel processing. The justification says it follows 'two GAO protests' and a protest submitted June 26, 2025, and the eight months also allows for further protests before the competitive follow-on order.

blocks.title: Transportation Department extends Deloitte's cybersecurity contract two months while it restructures its IT workforce
meta: Logical follow-on to a competitive order
blocks.text: The order expires October 31, 2026 and the extension runs through December 31. The justification says it is needed 'while DOT goes through the process of restructuring the Department's information technology workforce' and decides whether the support can be reduced or taken over by federal employees. Deloitte runs security operations, vulnerability management and compliance reporting under the order.

meta: Department of Veterans Affairs (Network Contract Office 01)
blocks.text: The statement of work for West Haven grounds and maintenance contains a link reading https://www.weather.gov/?utm_source=chatgpt.com, which is the tag ChatGPT adds to sources it cites. sections.headline: Two terminated contracts stand out: Social Security cancels a Dell hardware order and Veterans Affairs ends a hospital construction contract after a protest
paragraphs: There are 25 new awards of $2 million or more (1 Defense Department award just published after the 90-day hold), 5 large modifications and 3 cuts. The two larger Anthropic awards are today's Top Story. The 24 routine actions are listed with links in 'USAspending: Every Other New Award' at the end of the edition.

blocks.text: Dell Federal Systems L.P lost a hardware order: the Social Security Administration terminated for convenience a Splunk refreshment order under its server hardware contract, with a complete de-obligation of $7,177,428 on October 27. (award)

Semper Tek Inc had its remaining work ended on a Department of Veterans Affairs hospital repair contract: a unilateral modification dated October 26 terminated all remaining work 'for protest corrective action', removing $10,559,462. (award)

Axiom Space Inc got $12.5 million on October 23 from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration under delivery order 5 of its Exploration Extravehicular Activity Services contract, which covers production, testing, certification, delivery and repair of sortie suit hardware for exploration missions. It was tagged White House by the keyword match, but nothing in the record ties it to the Executive Office of the President. (award)

OCS Construction Services Inc won $3,053,599 from the General Services Administration on October 26 for courthouse hardening at the Edward R. Roybal and Los Angeles U.S. courthouses, plus anti-scale fencing on Alameda Street. (award)
